# French-language fightback as English colonises EU

Paris hopes to turn tide by providing courses for diplomats from new member states

Amelia Gentleman in Paris

Sun 11 Jul 2004 21.43 EDT

In a chateau near Avignon, ambassadors and senior government officials from Europe's newest member states have been brought together over breakfast to discuss French verbs.

The meeting is followed by several hours of one-on-one grammar drill and tutorials in telephone technique, before officials reunite for a crash course on the glories of French culture.

This linguistic boot camp for eastern Europe's diplomatic elite is one of the most innovative projects launched to date by France's Francophonie agency as part of its campaign to stem the decline of the French language.
